pillars.name: Getting started
pillars.summary: Where people who are new to AI or to code begin. Not part of DeepLearning.AI's map, which assumes you already build software.

skills.name: AI literacy
skills.summary: Knowing what AI can and can't do, and using AI tools well in your own work.

skills.name: Python basics
skills.summary: Writing and running simple Python programs, the language most AI courses use.

pillars.name: Building and deploying AI applications
pillars.summary: Turning unpredictable models into reliable systems by building, examining the results and deciding what to try next.

skills.name: LLM foundations
skills.summary: How LLMs work, when they fail, and how to choose, prompt, configure and adapt them.

skills.name: Grounding models with data
skills.summary: Giving models the right context: retrieval, knowledge graphs and documents turned into LLM-ready input.

skills.name: Building agentic systems
skills.summary: Workflows and agents with tools, memory and context management, made safe enough for production.

skills.name: Evaluation-driven development
skills.summary: A disciplined evals and error-analysis loop that shows what to improve next.

skills.name: Operating in production
skills.summary: Observability, release testing, and cost and latency for AI systems with real users.

skills.name: Machine learning foundations
skills.summary: Machine learning and deep learning: models, training, data and error analysis.

pillars.name: Software engineering fundamentals
pillars.summary: The software knowledge you need to steer coding agents toward the right tradeoffs.

skills.name: Building full-stack applications
skills.summary: Front end and back end: UI, APIs, state, persistence and testing.

skills.name: Managing data
skills.summary: Data models, storage and pipelines, kept clean, fresh, private and compliant.

skills.name: Designing system architectures
skills.summary: Choosing the architecture and stack, and evolving them from prototype to scale.

skills.name: Making systems secure and reliable
skills.summary: Testing strategy, designing around failure and building security in from the start.

skills.name: Scaling and operating in production
skills.summary: Deployment, CI/CD, monitoring and scaling for real traffic.

pillars.name: Using coding agents
pillars.summary: Directing and customizing coding agents while keeping control of what gets built.

skills.name: Directing the workflow
skills.summary: Planning, writing specs and splitting work into steps an agent can build and you can verify.

skills.name: Enabling agent autonomy
skills.summary: Choosing how much to delegate, running agents in parallel and setting safe permissions.

skills.name: Reviewing the work
skills.summary: Testing and reviewing what agents produce, including AI code review.

skills.name: Customizing the agent and its environment
skills.summary: Skills, memory, hooks, MCP servers and standing context files.

skills.name: Coding agent foundations
skills.summary: How coding agents work inside, so you can spot their failure modes.

pillars.name: Shaping the build
pillars.summary: Owning projects end to end with product sense, fast build loops and leadership.

skills.name: Driving the build loop
skills.summary: Prototypes and MVPs that test an idea fast and decide the next step.

skills.name: Making product decisions
skills.summary: Product and business sense, and user empathy grounded in research and metrics.

skills.name: Communicating and leading
skills.summary: Aligning stakeholders and helping an organization understand what AI can do.

skills.name: High agency ownership
skills.summary: Driving projects end to end, acting in ambiguity and measuring work by its value.

gaps.ownership: No DeepLearning.AI course teaches this directly yet.
